questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: The history of swimming and attitudes to it
How to teach young children to swim safely
The best beaches in the Maldives
Lord Byron's life as a poet
questions.why: Neil says this programme is on the history of swimming, which is more than just exercise.

options: To win competitions
Because her doctor told her to
For exercise and to relax
To get to work
questions.why: She says she enjoys swimming for exercise and to relax.

questions.q: What did Lord Byron do in 1810?
options: He built a large public swimming pool in Istanbul
He banned people from swimming in the sea near his home
He wrote a long book about the history of Roman baths
He swam across the water between Europe and Asia
questions.why: Neil says in 1810 he swam the Hellespont, which separates Europe from Asia.

questions.q: What happened to swimming in Europe after the Roman Empire declined?
options: It became a popular sport
It lost its appeal
It was only allowed in temples
It was taught in schools
questions.why: Neil says swimming seems to have lost its appeal in Europe after the decline of the Roman Empire.

questions.q: According to Professor Kevin Dawson, why did the Church discourage swimming?
options: Water seemed unsafe and nude swimming immodest
Swimming took people away from church on Sundays
There were not enough lakes
It was too expensive for ordinary people
questions.why: He says water was seen as unsafe and unnatural, and swimming nude was felt to be immodest.

questions.q: Why could people in the Maldives be world leaders in swimming, according to Mikael Rosen?
options: They have the best swimming coaches
They swim to school every day
The government pays them to swim
Most live close to a warm lagoon
questions.why: He says most citizens have half a mile to a lukewarm lagoon.

questions.q: Why did swimming become disapproved of in the Maldives in the 1960s?
options: The lagoons became polluted by boats and hotels
Teachers from abroad saw students missing school to swim
Too many children drowned in the sea every year
The government built too many public swimming pools
questions.why: He says teachers from India and Sri Lanka noticed students playing hooky in the lagoons.

questions.q: What does Neil think about what happened in the Maldives?
options: It was the right decision for the students
The students should have been punished more
It was unfair, given the local swimming culture
The teachers understood the water culture well
questions.why: Neil says it seems a bit unfair since there was already a strong swimming culture there.
